summary: A 1970 BLM fire report lists a manned lookout at Gordon Lyon Peak near Anchorage; no source describes the lookout today.

facts.status_note: Only a 1970 report describes a lookout on this peak; no source says whether any structure stands today.

access.note: The National Park Service lists the Nike Site Summit missile site on the peak as not open to the public. A volunteer group gives guided summer tours. The sources do not describe access to the 1970 lookout.

events.note: Alaska Fire Report lists Gordon Lyon Peak among the lookouts manned in the Anchorage-Palmer area that year.

notes_for_editor: The only source for a lookout on this peak is one line in the 1970 BLM report: 'Still others were manned at ... Gordon Lyon Peak'. It does not say what kind of structure stood there or where on the mountain. The NPS describes Nike Site Summit, an Army missile battery activated on Mount Gordon Lyon in 1959 and closed in 1979. The sources do not say whether the 1970 lookout was on the missile site, so the story keeps the two apart and does not link them. The brief's kind 'unknown' and the status 'unknown' stay as they are; the 'staffed' event matches the report's 'manned'. The NPS page lists the Nike site as not open to the public; a Friends of Nike Site Summit page (not read) says 2026 tours were fully booked as of 5 July 2026, which was seen only in a search snippet and is not cited. The JBER Nike page and Alaska Magazine returned 403 and were not used. Two web searches were used on this record (a third search was not run). The brief's 'Anchorage Borough' is used as given in the brief.
